# HW4 Overview

**Due: Friday, November 20 (11:59 PM Chicago Time) **

In this last assignment before the final project, you will practice the programming techniques from Lectures 12–15.


### Accessing the repo

1. Go to **[this link](https://classroom50.org/css-fall26/css/assignments/hw04/accept)**. The first time, click *Sign in with GitHub* and authorize Classroom 50 (the tool we use to distribute assignments).

2. Click *Accept assignment* to create your private `hw04` repository on GitHub. Your repository will be named `css-hw04-<USERNAME>`. Keep the page open until the setup checklist finishes (a few seconds).

3. Click *Open repository* to access it.

If the page says *"Not a member yet"*, accept the invitation to our GitHub organization (check your email, including spam), then click *Check again*. If it says *"This assignment isn't available to you"*, contact the instructor.


### Cloning the repo into your Workbench

1. Log into *Workbench* and start a new project:  
   *File > New Project > Version Control > Git*

2. In the *Repository URL* field:
   - Paste the URL of your GitHub repository. To find the URL, go to your `hw04` repo on GitHub, click the green Code button, and copy the SSH or HTTPS link (use the method you configured during setup: Workbench users must select SSH).
   - The project name should auto-fill. If not, type the same name manually (it should match the GitHub repo name).

3. Choose where to save the project directory locally. *Tip:* Avoid moving folders after cloning them.  
4. Check the box *"Open in new session"* (recommended for keeping projects organized).

5. Click *Create Project*. This will:
   - Create a new folder on your machine  
   - Initialize a Git repository linked to GitHub  
   - Open an RStudio Project in a new session

You’ll use this same process to access and set up each homework assignment throughout the course.


### General Homework Workflow

See [Homework 1](hw01.qmd) for details. The workflow is the same for all assignments.


# HW4 Description

In this homework assignment, you will practice the programming concepts we covered in recent lectures through guided exercises. All the details can be found in this repository.

::: {.callout-note}

- Homework for this class are designed to be completed over multiple sessions. Start early, and remember to save, commit, and push your work regularly.

- Do not use AI tools to generate R code from scratch or to think for you; that defeats the purpose of the assignment and violates our class policy on plagiarism. You may use AI to debug after trying on your own. Only submit code you fully understand. Reach out if you have questions, we are here to help!

:::


# Formatting Guide for All Homework

See [Homework 2](hw02.qmd) for details. The formatting expectations are the same for all assignments.


# Submit the Assignment

To submit your assignment on Canvas, follow these steps:

1. Before the deadline, push the final version of your work to your GitHub repository. *Tip:* don’t wait until the end to make your first commit; instead stage, commit, and push your work regularly as you go.

   Your GitHub repository should include:
   - `programming.Rmd`: main file you will work on
   - `programming.md`: you will generate this file from the `.Rmd` by simply knitting it
   - the folder that contains the graphs that you generated in your `.Rmd`, if any

2. When you're ready to submit:
   - Copy the URL of your GitHub repository. It will look something like: `https://github.com/css-fall26/css-hw04-yourusername`
   - Submit that URL on Canvas under HW04. Do not upload any files to Canvas. We only need the repository link. Your repository remains private, only the instructional staff can access it.
